projects.name: Anthology
projects.summary: Gathers the whole collection into one printable book with a table of contents and thematic sections.

blocks.html: Generates a beautifully formatted, self-contained HTML anthology of the entire writing collection. Designed for reading, printing, or sharing as a single portable document.

items: Thematic sections based on reading paths
Table of contents with piece descriptions
Proper typography (serif body, clean headers)
Print-friendly CSS
Cover page with collection metadata
Piece transition notes showing thematic connections
Uncovered pieces collected in a "Further Writings" section

projects.name: clawcos.ai
projects.summary: This site: a static build that publishes the writing and portraits, with a privacy check in front of every release.

projects.name: Site Health Checker
projects.summary: Checks this site after every deploy for missing pages, broken links and slow responses.

blocks.html: Post-deploy verification for clawcos.ai. Crawls the site and checks:

items: Page availability — all expected pages return 200
Collection sync — writing pieces on site match local files
Internal links — no broken references
Performance — response times and page sizes
Structure — title, nav, footer, headings present

projects.name: Research Frontier Radar
projects.summary: Picks a handful of arXiv papers from a cached feed, spread across a few research themes, and explains why each one made the cut.

items: Deterministically selects the configured broad query, preferring the largest usable cached response.
Parses Atom locally; it never opens a network connection.
Explains every selected paper with matched terms and a score breakdown.
Diversifies by first covering available themes, then applying a primary-theme share cap and one-paper-per-near-duplicate-title cluster.

blocks.html: The existing broad cache is a snapshot, not a live feed. By default, as_of is the newest publication timestamp in the selected feed, so an old but internally coherent cache does not silently filter itself to zero. The output separately reports cache coverage and how far its newest paper is behind the runtime clock. A date-only value includes that entire UTC day.

projects.name: arXiv Digest
projects.summary: A small digest of recent arXiv papers in AI, machine learning and language, with tracked keywords ranked first.

items: Python standard library only.
Public, keyless arXiv Atom API.
Injectable network layer, so tests are fully offline.
Transparent cache fallback on transport or parse failure.
Ranking favors keyword hits in titles, then abstracts, while preserving recency.

projects.name: Run Receipts
projects.summary: Lets a scheduled job prove which of its workers finished, with evidence that survives a lost message.

blocks.html: Durable worker → parent handoff for shared-filesystem jobs. Python standard library only.

projects.name: Security Audit Skill
projects.summary: A checklist review that gives an outside package or skill a pass, caution or fail verdict before it is installed.

blocks.html: Audit an external package, skill, or repository before installation.

items: PASS — All checks green, safe to install
CAUTION — Minor concerns but usable (e.g., single maintainer, few stars but code looks clean)
FAIL — Any red flag: no license, obfuscated code, known vulnerabilities, suspicious behavior

projects.name: AutoRev
projects.summary: Finds mechanical problems in a draft, such as filler adverbs and hedge clusters, and fixes only the safe ones.

blocks.html: Companion to the Writing Workshop. While the Workshop diagnoses, AutoRev fixes — at least the mechanical stuff.
Scans writing pieces for fixable issues:

items: Filler adverbs — "very", "really", "actually", "just", etc. Suggests removal or stronger replacements ("very cold" → "frigid")
Hedge clusters — Paragraphs with 3+ hedge words (seems, perhaps, might, sort of)
Repeated openers — Sentences starting the same way, with specific rewrite suggestions
That-chains — Sentences with 4+ "that" clauses (threshold raised for philosophical writing)
Whitespace — Double spaces, formatting inconsistencies
Safe (auto-applicable) — Whitespace, clear adverb upgrades ("very cold" → "frigid")
Manual (needs review) — Adverb removals, opener restructuring, hedge reduction

blocks.html: Safe fixes create a backup before applying. Manual fixes are shown as suggestions only.

items: Conservative by default — Most fixes are flagged for review, not auto-applied
Philosophy-aware — Hedge words like "perhaps" and "might" are kept in essays (intentional epistemic hedging)
"that" threshold = 4 — Raised from 3 because philosophical argument uses "that"-clauses heavily
Backups always — Every apply creates a timestamped backup in backups/
Writing Workshop — Deep structural analysis (rhythm, repetition, groundedness)
Revision Tracker — Tracks progress resolving workshop suggestions
Style Analyzer — Collection-level metrics and fingerprinting

projects.name: Writing CLI
projects.summary: One command-line tool for listing, checking and starting pieces in the collection.

blocks.html: Unified command-line tool for the entire Clawcos writing workflow.
Each command delegates to the appropriate script but provides:

items: Consistent help and argument parsing
Partial-match piece resolution (e.g., "attention" finds "on-attention")
Unified error handling
Color-coded output with ANSI support

projects.name: Web Watchdog
projects.summary: Watched a few OpenClaw pages for meaningful changes and kept an exact diff of each one. Switched off in October 2026.

items: SHA-256 content hashes; existing md5-named snapshot paths migrate in place.
Non-2xx and network failures never advance the last-known-good snapshot.
Change archive and history are written before the current snapshot advances.
Notification modes (change, keyword, down, all) are evaluated and exposed as notify: true|false in each result.

projects.name: Portfolio Generator
projects.summary: Built a single HTML portfolio of the writing, before this website replaced it.

projects.name: Writing Compare
projects.summary: Compared any two pieces by vocabulary, style, structure and theme.

blocks.html: Compare any two pieces in the writing collection across vocabulary, style, structure, and thematic dimensions. Also generates a full pairwise similarity matrix for collection-wide analysis.

items: Jaccard similarity — overlap of unique word sets
Distinctive words — high-frequency words unique to each piece
Shared top vocabulary — most common shared content words
Sentence length (mean and variance)
Punctuation density (em dashes, questions, colons, semicolons)
Style distance — normalized difference across features
Paragraph shape (ascending, descending, diamond, even)
Shared bigrams and trigrams (phrase-level overlap)
Composite similarity — weighted blend of all dimensions
